issues.description: Constructor parameter order for class Lecture differs between the problem specification and the solution. The problem statement and UML require the constructor parameters in the order: lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors (see UML and constructor instructions in problem_statement.md). The solution implementation declares the constructor as: public Lecture(String lectureName, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents) (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 13). This mismatch can confuse students about the expected constructor signature and lead to inconsistent implementations or failing tests that assume the UML order.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor parameter order consistent with the UML and problem description. Recommended: change the solution's constructor signature to: public Lecture(String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors) and assign fields in that order. Alternatively, if the solution's order is intentional, update the problem statement/UML to document the constructor parameter order and update the template to show the intended signature so students are not confused.
